newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmen head disbands Turkmen-Russian gas venture.
newsitem.headline: Turkmen head disbands Turkmen-Russian gas venture.

text.p: Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov has signed a decree disbanding the Turkmen-Russian joint venture Turkmenrosgaz, which transported Turkmen natural gas to former Soviet republics, an energy official said on Wednesday.

An official in state oil and gas company Turkmanneftegaz told Reuters the venture, in which Turkmenneftegaz had 51 percent, Russian gas monopoly Gazprom 45 percent and U.S. firm Itera four percent, was taken due to what he called its poor economic activity.
"The activity of this venture was considered unnecessary because in practice it did not work," he said.
Itera could not be reached for immediate comment.

The venture was formed in January last year in line with Niyazov's decree and transported Turkmen natural gas to consumers in energy-starved ex-Soviet republics, mostly Ukraine, via Russian pipelines.
Under the deal, Itera undertook an obligation to pay Turkmenistan $42 per cubic metre of natural gas.

Ukraine's Ambassador to Turkmenistan, Vadim Chuprun, told Reuters on Tuesday Itera owed Turkmenistan around $200 million for gas transported to Ukraine in 1996 and another $120 million in cash and $117 million in goods for deliveries made in 1997.
